texts.preamble: Poonamchand Joshi vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 15 May, 2024 Author: Vishal Mishra Bench: Vishal Mishra
texts.facts: 2. It is the case of the petitioner that on 31.01.2013, the Food Inspector conducted inspection of a Paan shop of the petitioner and seven retail packs of restricted Rajshree Gutka was found. They were seized. On 06.03.2014 a complaint was filed against the petitioner for offence under Section 3(1) (zx), 26(2)(i)(ii)(v) read with Section 51, 52(i) and 59(i) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 and Regulation 2.3.4 of the Food Safety and Standards (Prohibition and Restriction on Sales) Regulation, 2011. 3. The learned Magistrate has taken cognizance on the complaint on 06.03.2014 and issued summons for the presence of the accused. The accused filed an application under Section 77 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 raising a specific objection that as per Section 77 of the Act of 2006, the Court cannot take cognizance of the offence after one year from the date of commission of offence, therefore, prayed for discharging of the accused. No 2 MCRC-50185-2021 reply was filed by the respondent. They have orally opposed the same. 4. The learned Trial Court on 27.07.2017 already framed charges in the matter, therefore, it was observed that the petitioner is already protected and his objection will be considered after recording of evidence.
texts.arguments: Poonamchand Joshi vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 15 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141754709/ 1 5. It is his case that a specific time limit for prosecution is provided in terms of Section 77 of the Act of 2006 wherein it is specifically provided that no Court shall take cognizance of an offence under this Act after the expiry of the period of one year from the date of commission of an offence. It is argued that Section 77 contains non-obstante clause and it specifically bars the Court from taking cognizance and a complaint is made after a period of one year. It is his case that the inspection of the shop was carried out on 31.03.2013 and complaint was filed on 06.03.2014 that is admittedly after a period of one year from the date of commission of offence. 6. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent has vehemently opposed the application and has supported the order passed by the learned Trial Court for taking cognizance in the matter. It is argued that under Section 77 of the Act of 2006 a proviso is there which provides for extending period upto three years. The learned Trial Court has considered the application filed by the petitioner and it was pointed out that cognizance was already taken on 06.03.2014. No objections were raised at the relevant time. The complainant evidence has already been recorded in the matter. The case is listed for recording defence evidence and rejected the application. It is argued that there is nothing on record to show that cognizance in the matter could not have been taken or whether the Commissioner has granted permission to lodge a prosecution after expiry of one year. No document pertaining to the same is available on record. The matter was placed before the concerned authority for taking sanction for 3 MCRC-50185-2021 prosecution and on 16.01.2014, the sanction was granted. Immediately thereafter the matter was placed before the concerned Court. There is no illegality. He has prayed for dismissal of the petition. The same reads as under :- "77. Time limit for prosecution:- Notwithstanding anything contained in this Act, no Court shall take cognizance of an offence under this Act after the expiry of the period of one year from the date of commission of an offence Provided that the Commissioner of Food Safety may for the reasons to be recorded in writing, approve prosecution within an extended period of upto three years." 9. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of State of Punjab Vs. Sarwan Singh reported in AIR 1981 SC 1054 has clearly held that bar of limitation on prosecution was to prevent the parties from filing cases after a long time, as a result of which material evidence may disappear and to prevent the abuse of the process of the Court by filing vexatious and belated prosecutions after a long delay.
